newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghanistan's Taleban criticise Non-Aligned group.
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan's Taleban criticise Non-Aligned group.

text.p: A senior member of the Taleban administration on Monday criticised the Non-Aligned Movement for inviting a representative of the ousted Afghan govennment of President Burhanuddin Rabbani to its meeting in New Delhi.

"Whoever considers Rabbani's representative as the representative of the Islamic State of Afghanistan is making a big mistake," Amir Khan Mutaqi, acting Information Minister in the Taleban administration, told journalists on Monday.

"If there is a necessity for the representative of the country to take part in the conference, it should be the representative of the Islamic State of Afghanistan (the Taleban) since it is the representative of the nation," he said.
The Taleban, who captured Kabul last September and control about 75 per cent of Afghanistan, have yet to be recognised as the legitimate government by any other nation or international body.
Afghanistan's seat in the United Nations is occupied by a representative of Rabbani's ousted administration.
Mutaqi accused India, the hosts of the two-day Non-Aligned Movement meeting, of helping the Afghan opposition.
"We are sure that India supports Rabbani. It gives good advice in political activities and it helped Rabbani when he was in power with technicians to repair his planes," he said.
"Our demand for India is that anyone who is a rebel should be considered as a rebel and a government be considered as a government," Mutaqi added.
